rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject is humankind generally; the following plural most of them supports a generic, rather than individual, reference.
rows.anchor: وهذا ظاهر في أن المراد بالإنسان الجنس غذ لو أريد العهد لقيل لكنه لا يعلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative identifies the person as Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالإنسان حذيفة بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalnāhu means We bestowed the blessing on him as a favor.
rows.anchor: أي أعطيناه إياها تفضلا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some restrict takhwīl to gifts given freely, not recompense.
rows.anchor: فإن التخويل على ما قيل مختص به لا يطلق على ما أعطى جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boast may mean the recipient knew how to earn the blessing, knew he deserved it, or knew God knew he merited it.
rows.anchor: على علم مني بوجوه كسبه أو بأني سأعطاه لمالي من الإستحقاق أو على علم من الله تعالى بي وباستيجابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innamā makes the boast exclusive: he claims he received it only because of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وإنما للحصر أي ما أوتيته لشيء من الأشياء إلا لأجل علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the blessing; its masculine form is explained by construing the feminine blessing as a thing, a verbal noun, wealth, or by masculine predominance.
rows.anchor: والهاء للنعمة والتذكير لتأوليها بشيء من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible reading treats innamā as a relative expression, meaning what I received is based on knowledge; al-Ālūsī deems it unlikely because the Qurʾānic spelling joins it.
rows.anchor: ويبعد موصوليتها كتابتها متصلة في المصاحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuttal says the blessing is a trial testing whether its recipient gives thanks or is ungrateful.
rows.anchor: بل ما أوتيه امتحان له أيشكر أم يكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun may follow the word niʿmah after its meaning was considered first; alternatives make it agree with the predicate or refer to the act of granting.
rows.anchor: والضمير للنعمة باعتبار لفظها كما أن الأول لها باعتبار معناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with masculine agreement still refers to the blessing, or alternatively to the act of giving.
rows.anchor: وقريء بالتذكير فهو للنعمة أيضا كالذي مر أو للإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the blessing a trial, though it is an instrument of testing, intensifies the expression.
rows.anchor: أخبر عنه بالفتنة مع أنه آلهة لها لقصد المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from the human singular to most of them confirms that al-insān is generic; making it a specific person here would require a strained pronoun shift.
rows.anchor: وإرادة العهد هناك وإرجاع الضمير للمطلق هنا على أنه استخدام نظير عندي درهم ونصفه تكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa links this response to the preceding account of aversion to mentioning God alone: in distress they call the very God whose mention they shunned, rather than the idols they welcomed.
rows.anchor: حيث أنهم يشمئزون عن ذكر الله تعالى وحده ويستبشرون بذكر الآلهة فإذا مسهم ضر دعوا من اشمأزوا من ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is a mocking, rebuking connective that exposes their contradiction and reversal; al-Ālūsī compares it to someone who mistreats another but asks that person for help when needy.
rows.anchor: والغرض منه التهكم والتحميق وفيه ذمهم بالمناقضة والتعكيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the fa causally: mentioning the result entails its cause; this may repeat the next verse unless one occurrence is worldly and the other belongs to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن تكون للسببية داخلة على السبب لأن ذكر المسبب يقتضي ذكر سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the intervening clauses as parenthetical and strengthening the censure; Abū Ḥayyān calls this strained and Abū ʿAlī rejects parentheticals of two clauses, but al-Ālūsī defends the construction with Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو حيان أن في ذلك تكلفا واعتراضا بأكثر من جملتين وأبو علي الفارسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the preceding sentence, innamā ūtītuhu ʿalā ʿilm; a masculine reading instead means the statement or speech.
rows.anchor: ضمير ( قالها ) لقوله تعالى : ( إنما أوتيته على علم ) لأنها كلمة أو جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those before them are Qarun and his people; attributing what Qarun said to the whole group is a rational metaphor.
rows.anchor: والذين من قبلهم قارون وقومه فإنه قال ورضوا به فالإسناد من باب إسناد ما للبعض إلى الكل وهو مجاز عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the ظرف figurative: the saying became widespread among them, whether as the same wording or an equivalent saying.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون التجوز في الظرف فقالها الذين من قبلهم بمعنى شاعت فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their accumulated earnings and worldly possessions did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: من متاع الدنيا ويجمعون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene details how the disbelievers are fully requited and how that requital occurs.
rows.anchor: الخ تفصيل للتوفية وبيان لكيفيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Driving them implies forceful, urgent movement; here it conveys humiliation as they are driven in successive groups.
rows.anchor: والسوق يقتضي الحث على المسير بعنف وإزعاج وهو الغالب ويشعر بالإهانة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines zumrah as a small group and relates the word to sparse hair or scant manliness.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : هي الجماعة القليلة ومنه شاة زمرة قليلة الشعر ورجل زمر قليل المروءة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another derivation connects zumrah to sound, since a group is rarely without it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم اشتقاق الزمرة من الزمر وهو الصوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The groups follow one another, ordered according to their degrees of error and wickedness.
rows.anchor: أفواجا متفرقة بعضها في أثر بعض مترتبة حسب ترتب طبقاتهم في الضلالة والشرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell’s gates had remained shut until the condemned arrived, like prison doors, and close after they enter.
rows.anchor: وكانت قبل مجيئهم غير مفتوحة فهي كسائر أبواب السجون لا تزال مغلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More than one reader recites the verb with doubled tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ غير واحد ( فتحت ) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers’ question is a reproach and rebuke.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التقريع والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were of the condemned people’s kind, so they could understand the message and readily consult them.
rows.anchor: أي من جنسكم تفهمون ما ينبؤنكم به ويسهل عليكم مراجعتهم

rows.speaker: ابن هرمز
rows.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads the verb with feminine tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز ( تأتكم ) بتاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has nudhur in place of rusul.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( نذر منكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses recited to them were revealed for their benefit.
rows.anchor: المنزلة لمصلحتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is most clearly the time of entering the Fire, since the actual warning concerns punishment and its time; it may instead mean Resurrection, which includes this time or their particular punishment.
rows.anchor: أي وقتكم هذا وهو وقت دخولكم النار لأن المنذر به الحقيقة العذاب ووقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is cited against moral obligation before revealed law: the condemned are rebuked for disbelief after messengers conveyed law and warned them.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على أنه لا تكليف قبل الشرع وبخوهم بكفرهم بعد تبليغ الرسل للشرائع وإنذارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument is inferential and assumes disputed generality; rational-duty proponents can say post-message disbelief merits sharper rebuke, while the verbs rule out interpreting the messengers as intellect.
rows.anchor: هو دليل إقناعي لأنه إنما يتم على اعتبار المفهوم وعموم الذين كفروا وكلاهما محل نزاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word of punishment is God’s decree that they are wretched and among the people of the Fire for their bad choice, or His statement to Iblis about filling Hell with him and his followers.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها الحكم عليهم بالشقاوة وأنهم من أهل النار لسوء اختيارهم أو قوله تعالى لإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them disbelievers instead of using a pronoun hints that disbelief is the cause of the punishment; their reply is admission, not an excuse.
rows.anchor: ووضعوا الكافرين موضع ضميرهم للإيماء إلى علية الكفر والكلام اعتراف لا اعتذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Pharaoh resolved to kill Moses, his advisers restrained him, saying Moses was no real danger, only a sorcerer matched by another sorcerer, and killing him would suggest Pharaoh could not answer his proofs.
rows.anchor: كفوه بقولهم : ليس بالذي تخافه وهو أقل من ذلك وأضعف وما هو إلا ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Pharaoh knew Moses was a prophet, yet was crafty and bloodthirsty; fear of immediate destruction restrained him, while let me kill him pretended to his people that they were holding him back.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه لعنه الله تعالى استيقن أنه عليه السلام نبي ولكن كان فيه خب وجربزة وكان قتالا سفاكا للدماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request to be left alone masks Pharaoh’s own inner fear; his apparent restraint by others was a pretense.
rows.anchor: وما كان ييكفه إلا ما في نفسه من هول الفزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase outwardly belittles Moses by challenging him to call his Lord, while betraying Pharaoh’s terror of that prayer.
rows.anchor: بدعائه ربه سبحانه كما يقال : ادع ناصرك فإني منتقم منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt may be sarcastic, or spoken in earnest; either way, one claiming to be their highest lord should not treat Moses’ claim as weighty.
rows.anchor: فما لمن يدعي أنه ربهم الأعلى أن يجعل لما يدعيه موسى عليه السلام وزنا فيتفوه به تهكما أو حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means Moses could change their religious condition of worshipping Pharaoh and idols, which Pharaoh had ordered them to carve and treat as intercessors.
rows.anchor: أن يغير حالكم الذي أنتم عليه من عبادتي وعبادة الأصنام وكان عليه اللعنة قد أمرهم بنحتها وإن تجعل شفعاء لهم عنده

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes dīn here to mean political authority or sovereignty; Pharaoh fears Moses will change their rule and subjugate them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : الدين سلطان ومنه قول زهير : لئن حللت بحي من بني أسد

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Moses cannot replace their religion entirely, Pharaoh says he may cause worldly disorder through conflict, lost security, disrupted livelihoods, killing, and displacement.
rows.anchor: وذلك بالتهارج الذي يذهب معه إلا من وتتعطل المزارع والمكاسب ويهلك الناس قتلا وضياعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first account of dīn, the threat is harm to religious affairs by alteration or to worldly affairs by disruption; both would be bitter outcomes.
rows.anchor: أني أخاف أن يفسد عليكم أمر دينكم بالتبديل أو يفسد عليكم أمر دنياكم بالتعطيل وهما أمران كل منهما مر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says Pharaoh meant by corruption obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة أن اللعين عني بالفساد طاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The people of Medina and Abu ʿAmr read wa-an, with a connecting conjunction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو و ( وأن ) الواو الواصلة

rows.speaker: الأعرج والأعمش وابن وثاب وعيسى وابن كثير وابن عامر والكوفيون غير حفص
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the verb with fatḥah on yāʾ and hāʾ and read al-fasād in the nominative.
rows.anchor: حفص ( يظهر ) بفتح الياء والهاء ( الفساد ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads the verb with doubled ẓāʾ and hāʾ and al-fasād nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ( يظهر بتشديد الظاء والهاء

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads the verb passive, with al-fasād as nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ( يظهر ) بضم الياء وفتح الهاء مبنيا للمفعول ( الفساد ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported identifications make the believer a Copt and Pharaoh’s cousin or heir and police chief, an Israelite, or an outsider to both groups.
rows.anchor: قيل كان قبطيا ابن عم فرعون وكان يجري مجرى ولي العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Israelite or outsider identifications, he is called one of Pharaoh’s people because he entered their circle and concealed his faith by outwardly professing their religion from fear.
rows.anchor: ووصفه على هذين القولين بكونه من آل فرعون باعتبار دخوله في زمرتهم وإظهار أنه على دينهم وملتهم تقية وخوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse attaches min āli Firʿawn to concealing his faith, restricting the concealed believer to Pharaoh’s household rather than Moses’ followers; stopping after believer is then possible.
rows.anchor: على القولين متعلق بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection says katama takes a direct object, not min; al-Ālūsī answers that lexicographers allow min with its first object, though the adjective attachment is more apparent.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأن كتم يتعدى بنفسه دون من فيقال : كتمت فلانا كذا دون كتمت من فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent parse makes the phrase a second adjective of the man and takes his descent from Pharaoh’s family literally.
rows.anchor: نعم تعلقه بذلك خلاف الظاهر بل الظاهر تعلقه بمحذوف وقع صفة ثانية لرجل والظاهر على هذا كونه من آل فرعون حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer is variously named Shamaʿan, Kharbil, Hizbil, or Habib.
rows.anchor: واسمه قيل : شمعان بشين معجمة وقيل : خربيل بخاء معجمة مكسورة وراء مهملة ساكنة

rows.speaker: عيسى وعبد الوارث وعبيد بن عقيل وحمزة بن القاسم عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: These authorities read rajul with a still jīm, a dialect of Tamim and Najd.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وعبد الوارث وعبيد بن عقيل وحمزة بن القاسم عن أبي عمرو ( رجل ) بسكون الجيم وهي لغة تميم ونجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means are you intending to kill him: it names the result, killing, while intending is the cause; its interrogative force does not require an actual killing.
rows.anchor: أي أتقصدون قتله فهو مجاز ذكر فيه المسبب وأريد السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means because he says my Lord is God.
rows.anchor: أي لأن يقول ذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows an omitted time noun, meaning would you kill him at the moment you hear him speak, without examining his case.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كون ( أن يقول ) على تقدير مضاف أي وقت أن يقول فحذف الظرف

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that a complement standing for a temporal noun must be an explicit verbal noun or a durative mā clause, not the non-explicit أن construction.
rows.anchor: ورده أبو حيان بأن القائم مقام الظرف لا يكون إلا المصدر الصريح كجئت صياح الديك أو ما كان بما الدوامية

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni, like al-Zamakhshari, expressly permits the proposed construction; al-Ālūsī says this settles the objection.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن ابن جني كالزمخشري صرح بالجواز وكل إمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proofs comprise the miracles and numerous arguments that attest Moses’ truthfulness; the circumstantial clause may describe the killer or the man killed.
rows.anchor: الشاهدة على صدقه من المعجزات والاستدلالات الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound feminine plural can convey abundance when definite, as the context supports here.
rows.anchor: وجمع المؤنث السالم وإن شاع أنه للقلة لكنه إذا دخلت عليه أل يفيد الكثرة بمعونة المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Lord of all of them gently draws them toward admitting that Moses’ Lord is their Lord too.
rows.anchor: أي من عند من نسب إليه الربوبية وهو ربكم لا ربه وحده وهذا استدراج إلى الأعتراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer reasons that saying my Lord is God, or their saying our lord is Pharaoh, warrants no killing; since Moses names their true Lord too, he deserves respect, not betrayal.
rows.anchor: وفي ( أن يقول ربي الله إلى من ربكم ) نكتة جليلة وهي أن من يقول ربي الله أو فلان لا يقتضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cautious believer says that if Moses lies, the burden of his lie falls on him and there is no need to kill him to avert it.
rows.anchor: لا يتخطاه وبال كذبه فيحتاج في دفعه إلى قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a partial fulfillment of Moses’ warning would be dangerous; warning against a part implies that the whole would be worse, while also sounding fair-minded.
rows.anchor: فلا أقل من أن يصيبكم بعض الذي يعدكم أو يعدكموه وفيه مبالغة في التحذير فإنه إذا حذرهم من إصابة البعض أفاد أنه مهلك مخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the part as a worldly punishment, one of Moses’ promised punishments and the one more plausibly expected by Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد يصبكم ما يعدكم من عذاب الدنيا وهو بعض مواعيده كأنه خوفهم بما هو أظهر احتمالا عندهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda allows baʿḍ to mean all and cites Labid’s verse; al-Ālūsī notes that the verse is better read literally as referring to the death of one’s own self.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة أنه فسر البعض بالكل أيضا وأنشد قول لبيد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sharply criticizes Abu ʿUbayda’s interpretation if the report attributing it to him is sound.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : إن صحت الرواية عن أبي عبيدة في ذلك فقد حق فيه قول المازني

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj keeps baʿḍ in its ordinary sense: the believer establishes an unanswerable proof and shows the merit of deliberation over haste.
rows.anchor: وذهب الزجاج إلى أن ( بعض ) فيه على ظاهره والمراد إلزام الحجة وإبانة فضل المتأني على المستعجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The maxim that baʿḍ can mean all is not established by the cited poetry; in Labid’s line, some souls means the speaker himself, so the ordinary partitive meaning remains.
rows.anchor: على أن البعض فيه على ظاهره والمراد به نفسه

rows.speaker: عمرو القطامي
rows.claim: The patient person’s attaining some need is cited in discussion of whether baʿḍ means all; al-Ālūsī treats the line as supporting the literal-part reading.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا لذلك قول عمرو القطامي : قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته وقد يكون مع المستعجل الزلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poetic citation is offered for using baʿḍ to mean all, but al-Ālūsī says the wording does not require that sense.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا المجيء بمعنى كل قول الشاعر : إن الأمور إذا الأحداث دبرها دون الشيوخ فرى في بعضها خللا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer’s final argument has two readings: if Moses were an extravagant liar, God would not guide him to proofs and support him with miracles; or God would abandon and destroy him, leaving no need to kill him.
rows.anchor: احتجاج آخر ذو وجهين أحدهما أنه لو كان مسرفا كذابا لما هداه الله تعالى إلى البينات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man probably intends the first argument but hints at the second to soften his hearers; he indirectly calls Pharaoh extravagant in killing and corruption and a liar in claiming divinity.
rows.anchor: ولعله أراد الأول وأوهمهم أنه أراد الثاني لتلين شكيمتهم وعرض لفرعون بأنه مسرف أي في القتل والفساد كذاب في ادعاء الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final sentence may be attached to either conditional or to both.
rows.anchor: فالجملة مستأنفة متعلقة بالشرطية الأولى أو بالثانية أو بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the weak and the arrogant inhabitants of the Fire make this request when their arguments fail and their options narrow.
rows.anchor: من الضعفاء والمستكبرين جميعا لما ضاقت بهم الحيل وعيت بهم العلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the keepers of Jahannam rather than the keepers of the Fire intensifies the threat, since Jahannam is more specific and may denote the deepest pit.
rows.anchor: وكان الظاهر لخزنتها بضمير النار لكن وضع الظاهر موضعه للتهويل فإن جهنم أخص من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation places these disbelievers in Jahannam, the deepest level, and supposes its angels most likely to answer because of their greater nearness to God.
rows.anchor: أو لأنها محل لأشد العذاب الشامل للنار وغيرها وجوز أن يكون ذلك لبيان محل الكفرة في النار بأن تكون جهنم أبعد دركاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that those angels are assigned to the worst inmates and are presumed more responsive because of their closeness to God.
rows.anchor: فلعل الملائكة الموكلين بعذاب أولئك أجوب دعوة لزيادة قربهم من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask that one day’s measure, reckoned by worldly days, be removed from the punishment.
rows.anchor: أي مقدار يوم من أيام الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min can be explanatory or partitive; one parse omits the object of lighten and treats min al-ʿadhāb as its clarification.
rows.anchor: فمفعول ( يخفف ) محذوف و ( من ) تمل البيان والتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, day is the object with an omitted noun such as torment of a day, and from the punishment explains it: they ask to be spared one day of punishment.
rows.anchor: بحذف المضاف نحو ألم يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers ask whether messengers repeatedly came in worldly life with clear proofs of the evil outcome of disbelief and sins, reproaching the inmates for seeking more time and disabling the grounds for response.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا على الاستمرار بالحجج الواضحة الدالة على سوء مغبة ما كنتم عليه من الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit the messengers came and that they disbelieved them, as another verse states explicitly.
rows.anchor: أي أتونا بها فكذبناهم كما نطق به قوله تعالى : ( بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is explanatory ellipsis: since the inmates admit this, the keepers tell them to pray themselves, because the keepers cannot pray for those who acted as they did.
rows.anchor: فصيحة أي غذا كان الأمر كذلك فادعوا أنتم فإن الدعاء لمن يفعل فعلكم ذلك مستحيل صدوره عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative says the keepers were not authorized to pray for such people; al-Ālūsī rejects it because it does not explain the fa’s attribution of refusal to the inmates’ conduct and suggests permission could have changed matters.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في تعليل امتناع الخزنة عن الدعاء : لأنا لم نؤذن في الدعاء لأمثالكم وتعقب بأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers’ command is meant to make the inmates despair, not to raise hope of an answer.
rows.anchor: ولم يريدوا بأمرهم بالدعاء إطماعهم في الإجابة بل إقناطهم منها

words: وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers say the disbelievers’ prayer is futile and will not be answered.
rows.anchor: أي في ضياع وبطلان أي لا يجاب فهذه الجملة من كلام الخزنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the final sentence as God’s report to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي من كلامه تعالى إخبارا منه سبحانه لرسوله محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that a disbeliever’s prayer is never answered and that disbelievers cannot join the rain prayer; al-Ālūsī limits the verse to their prayer on Judgment Day, noting that worldly requests may be granted, whatever one calls that outcome.
rows.anchor: واستدل بها مطلقا من قال : إن دعاء الكافر لا يستجاب وأنه لا يمكن من الخروج في الاستسقاء والحق أن الآية في دعاء الكفار يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā ilā means to intend or turn toward a place without turning toward something else.
rows.anchor: أي قصد إليها وتوجه دون إرادة تأثير في غيرها من قولهم : استوى إلى مكان كذا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says istawā with ʿalā means mastery, as in the Throne verse; with ilā it means reaching or turning toward something, physically or through governance, with this verse an instance of the latter.
rows.anchor: وذكر الراغب أن الاستواء متى عدي بعلى فبمعنى الاستيلاء كقوله تعالى : ( الرحمن على العرش استوى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some construe the wording as elliptical, supplying creation: He then turned to create the heaven.
rows.anchor: أن في الكلام مضافا محذوفا أي ثم استوى إلى خلق السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Smoke is a dark, primordial material from which the heavens were composed; al-Ālūsī rejects indivisible atoms on the strength of arguments against them.
rows.anchor: أمر ظلماني ولعله أريد به مادتها التي تركبت وأنا لا أقول بالجواهر الفردة لقوة الأدلة على نفيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One cosmological report says the Throne was over water before creation; God heated the water, foam became earth, and rising smoke became the heavens.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن عرشه تعالى كان قبل خلق السماوات والأرض على الماء فأحدث الله تعالى في الماء سخونة فارتفع زبد ودخان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report begins with a red ruby that melted under the divine gaze into water, from which foam and smoke rose and creation followed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان هناك ياقوتة حمراء فنظر سبحانه إليها بعين الجلال فذابت وصارت ماء فأزبد وارتفع منه دخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The smoke did not derive from elemental fire: fire follows earth and may not yet have existed; even if it existed, no one claims the heavens formed from it. The philosophers’ celestial fire sphere is unreal, and meteors do not require it.
rows.anchor: فليس الدخان كائنا من النار التي هي إحدى العناصر لأنها من توابع الأرض ولم تكن موجودة غذ ذاك على قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one interpretation, the command means bringing out the benefits placed in heaven and earth, not their coming into existence; it is a command of subjugation, whose sequence must follow their preparation or the later summary.
rows.anchor: بما خلقت فيكما من المنافع فليس المعنى على إتيان ذاتهما وإيجادهما بل إتيان ما فيهما مما ذكر بمعنى إظهاره

rows.speaker: بعض
rows.claim: One proposed reordered construction places completion of the seven heavens before the command to heaven and earth; al-Ālūsī finds it less likely to invite dispute but contrary to the apparent order.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض : الكلام على التقديم والتأخير والأصل ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the command as an order to come into existence in a specified form and appointed time, making it a beginning of formation after the prior account of determination.
rows.anchor: أو كونا وإحداثا على وجه معين وفي وقت مقدر لكل منكما فالمراد إتيان ذاتهما وإيجادهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This formation reading is the one advanced by the author of Irshād al-ʿaql al-salīm and offered by others as a possibility; detailing earth and its provisions first highlights care for future human livelihood and urges faith.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه هو الذي قدمه صاحب الإرشاد وذكره غيره احتمالا وجعل الأمر عبارة عن تعلق إرادته تعالى بوجودهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the command represents God’s effective will through analogy with Be; there is no actual commander and commanded party.
rows.anchor: وجعل الأمر عبارة عن تعلق إرادته تعالى بوجودهما تعلقا فعليا بطريق التمثيل من غير أن يكون هناك آمر ومأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although both are addressed, heaven alone is named as the object of divine turning because the preceding account already specified the earth’s existence and contents.
rows.anchor: وخص الاستواء بالسماء مع أن الخطاب المترتب عليه متوجه إليهما معا اكتفاء بذكر تقدير الأرض وتقدير ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Willingly or unwillingly portrays the irresistible effect of divine power and the impossibility of resistance, not literal willingness or reluctance in the two entities.
rows.anchor: تمثيلا لتحتم تأثير قدرته تعالى فيهما واستحالة امتناعهما من ذلك لا إثبات الطوع والكره لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verbal nouns function adverbially, meaning obediently or reluctantly.
rows.anchor: وهما مصدران وقعا موقع الحال أي طائعتين أو كارهتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reply portrays complete responsiveness to divine power and their coming to be as commanded; obedience also presents their form as governed by profound wisdom.
rows.anchor: تمثيلا لكمال تأثرهما عن القدرة الربانية وحصولهما كما أمرا به وتصويرا لكون وجودهما كما هما عليه جاريا على مقتضى الحكمة البالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine sound plural is explained by their being addressed and answering; feminine agreement is unnecessary because their gender is grammatical only.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( طائعين ) يجمع المذكر السالم مع اختصاصه بالعقلاء باعتبار كونهما في معرض الخطاب والجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are signs in their origination, alternation, and each entering into the other.
rows.anchor: في حدوثهما وتعاقبهما وإيلاج كل منهما في الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are signs in their illumination and differences of light, size, and motions.
rows.anchor: في استنارتهما واختلافهما في قوة النور والعظم والحركات مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for mentioning night first is to signal its precedence, even though darkness is nonexistence.
rows.anchor: وقدم ذكر الليل قيل : تنبيها على تقدمه مع كون الظلمة عدما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun follows day because it is day’s sign and cause of its illumination, and because the moon’s light is said to derive from sunlight.
rows.anchor: وناسب ذكر الشمس بعد النهار لأنها آيته وسبب تنويره ولأنها أصل لنور القمر بناء على ما قالوا من أنه مستفاد من ضياء الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common view is that the sun’s light is not borrowed from another body; some attribute it to the Throne, while contemporary philosophers suspect another body and claim a small dark spot at the sun’s edge.
rows.anchor: وأما ضياؤها فالمشهور أنه غير طاريء عليها من جرم آخر وقيل : هو من العرش والفلاسفة اليوم يظنون أنه من جرم آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not worship the sun or moon because they are created things subjected to God’s will, like the worshippers themselves.
rows.anchor: لأنها من جملة مخلوقاته سبحانه وتعالى المسخرة علة وفق إرادته تعالى مثلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes the pronoun refer to all four signs; the sun and moon are primary objects of the command, while including night and day signals their lack of knowledge and choice.
rows.anchor: الضمير قيل للأربعة المذكورة والمقصود تعليق الفعل بالشمس والقمر لكن نظم معهما الليل والنهار إشعارا بأنهما من عداد ما لا يعلم ولا يختار

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says a nonrational plural takes feminine agreement, as in the examples about cutting the logs; this removes the need to explain the form by treating the signs as feminine.
rows.anchor: وحكم جماعة ما لا يعقل على ما قال الزمخشري حكم الأنثى فيقال : الأقلام بريتها وبريتهن

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan distinguishes small-number plurals, usually paired with singular feminine agreement, from abundance plurals, more eloquently paired with feminine plural agreement; he notes this form is not literally a small-number plural.
rows.anchor: نعم قال أبو حيان : ينبغي أن يفرق بين جمع القلة من ذلك وجمع الكثرة فإن الأفصح في الأول أن يكون بضمير الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposals limit the pronoun to the sun and moon, whose collective forms are nonrational plurals, or make it refer to the signs previously mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير للشمس والقمر والإئتان جمع وجمع ما لا يعقل يؤنث
